posts.name: Donner
posts.cooked:
We did great.  Worst game had Legacy down to 5 hp.  But we were crazy lucky w/ Iron Legacy.  Started with 2x Superhuman Redirection, 1x Galvanize, 1x Demoralizing Presence, 1x (whatever the armor is with Haka punching him).  Setback took out the armor with a Whoops!  Sorry! after Legacy played zero ongoing/equipments.  From there, Hypersonic Assaults, Offensive Transmutation, Throat Jab, and Heroic Interception, Iron Legacy couldn't do much.  He hurt us a lot at first, but that was it.

We were also really lucky with the Matriarch.  She got Huginn and Muninn out early, but she only played 2 or 3 birds each round for the first 3 rounds.

Wraith's Infrared Eyepieces have MVP for the games, keeping all the nasty cards at the bottom of the decks.

The Ennead starting out looking scary, but some unlucky plays on their part (deal one target damage, start a minor chain that goes nowhere) allowed us to get built up enough to burn Set down.  And then Hypersonic Assaults kept the Ennead down.  Scholar played 4x Keep Moving Forward for 3x Mortal Form to Energy and 1x Solid to Liquid and Get Out of the Way.  With Legacy with Inspiring Presence and Galvanize, the damage for that round was:

8 Ennead members (the rest were down) x 3 damage (Nuit was the second one down, so no damage reduction) = 24 damage from Get Out of the Way.  The Scholar healed 9 and then dealt three targets 11 damage apiece, wrecking the Ennead.  Then he used his base power to heal 2 and deal 3 targets 4 damage apiece.  For a total of 69 damage in one round.  Wraith then used Throwing Knives and Razor Ordinance to clean up the ones the Scholar left behind.

The rest of the games were pretty mild.  Gloomweaver was defeated once via Relics and once via damage.  Spite was killed both times on his front side from overwhelming damage (with damage prevention and deck control).  Citizen Dawn did not flip in the second fight.  Apostate was a joke with Wraith controlling the deck.  (I found it hilarious when Apostate played a round 1 Apocalypse and Setback tripped ("Whoops!  Sorry!", no other ongoing or equipment cards in play), breaking the end of the world.)

Anyway, we completed all 25 so far.  Although when I was submitting 14 games, I may have missed one or doubled up on another.

Fixer draws two cards.  Setback can still hit with Looking Up for four more after Legacy's boost.  AA draws two cards (his was the only bad hand, really).  Rook City plays Falling Statuary, hits a hero.  Iron Legacy HP = 26, no flip.  Plays another Demoralizing Presence, and much hitting commences.  The next turn was his end, however.  Legacy Plays inspring Presence, and boosts with his power.  Tempest uses Lightning Slash for a total of 8, then his power for 4.  IL HP = 14.  Mr. Fixer Charges for 4, then strikes for 3.  IL HP = 7.  Setback plays Reckless Rush, hits himself and IL for 4, then uses Looking Up for 5.  IL HP = -2.

posts.name: Jimeni
posts.cooked:
Well, I know I fell behind in reporting/writing my games out here (we were playing a lot faster than I could get around to writing), but my team has come to an end. Brutal Iron Legacy took us down. And it was brutal.

To be fair, we got much further than we expected. My wife and I rarely play advanced villains. We like being able to beat a villain several times (at least) on normal before moving to advanced, so I expected to quickly go down once the villains moved to advanced. But our "second-string" team of heroes proved to be way better than expected, and we plowed through some advanced villains (Some were very touugh that proved to be close battles, some weren't too bad at all).

And now we can say we've been victorious against Advanced Matriarch, and we've never even beat her on normal mode. :)

Anyway, it's been a lot of fun. Thanks, Pydro, for coming up with this and organizing it.

Some highlights: In the Akash'Bhuta battle at one point, Ra's Staff (6) had more hit points than Ra (4). (But we did some healing and hp management and we all came out alive). Omnitron X once destroyed all of Wraith's equipment (with her permission, of course) in a singularity in a desperate move to stop Blade from pulling the moon down. It worked, and we ended up killing him fairly easily once he flipped, but it was scary there for a bit on the first side.

This event gave us a chance to play some heroes who haven't gotten too much play from us, and we learned some fun combos and great ways to play heroes. Omnitron X certainly became a star in many of our battles. And Parse, who in the past had kinda proved underwhelming for us, showed her stuff, and we learned why people talk her up a lot.

So we had lots of fun, but our run is done.
And I'm a poet, and I did know it.

Thanks again!

Just ran rounds 2 & 3

Round 2: Legacy, Omnitron-X, Wraith, Setback, and Bunker vs. Kismet

This was one of the fastest games of SotM I have ever played. Kismet provided very little resistance, and was steamrolled in a few short rounds.

 

Round 3: Legacy, Omnitron-X, Wraith, Setback, and Bunker vs. The Dreamer

This one hurt. A lot. We managed to flip her fairly quickly, but after that, things got rough. We had 6 projections under the card, 4 in play, Setback incapped, and a total of 8 hp left among the other 4 heroes. As we went around the table, we picked off the Granite Oni and the Macabre Spectre, but had a Whipacorn and a Grotesque Arachnoid left at full health with only the incapacitated Setback and Bunker left to go....

Thanks to Legacy, we had Inspiring Presence and Galvanize in play. Bunker had Flak Cannon & Omni-Cannon in play, with Maintenance Unit & Turret Mode in hand. Setback inspired Bunker to shoot the Arachnoid with his Flak Cannon, taking it to 3 life remaining. Then, in his turn, Bunker fed his Maintenance Unit into the Omni-Cannon & went into Turret Mode. He fired the Omni-Cannon into the Arachnoid, killing it, and then hit the Whipacorn with his Flak Cannon, doing 6 damage. The Whipacorn still stood, at 1 hp remaining.

Things looked grim for our heroes, since they would not survive another round against the Dreamer's projections.

Then, from the local saloon, Matthew Hayes popped up and put a slug between the Whipacorn's eyes. "That thing'll look good mounted above my fireplace."

We had won...barely.

posts.name: Ario
posts.cooked:
My last game against the Matriarch went well, this game went beautifully. First turn she played Darken the Skies and her bird which destroys ongoings. Second turn she only gets two fowls out.  She doesn't get her second cohort until she was about the flip (fourth turn,) and up until that point she had been kept in check by offensive transmutations. And besides which how bad can a game be when Wraith starts with two impromtu inventions? The game ends with little to worry about (we were pecked a bit, but they saw their way through it,) and Scholar keeps Grace Under Fire against a fully targeted out Matriarch. 

But then we meet the Dreamer again... I wasn't looking forward to it after she destroyed me the first time, and barely let me get by on the redo, but what are you going to do?  The first part of the match goes well.  Another Grace Under Fire removes Dark Hero before his -2 reduction can become too much of an issue, a Whipacorn let Legacy play Heroic interception with no cost, and even when she flips the only hero with ongoings was the Naturalist and he recovers quickly. 

Even the flipside didn't start terrible, thanks to a meteor storm which cropped up.  Legacy used it's distraction to Take Down the Dreamer two turns in a row. It seemed like everything was bending over backwards to help me.  

Then her first turn at full damage and full card plays happen: five projections get out thanks to some violent nightmares, two macarbe specters (skeleton fellows, yes?) a samurai oni, and more besides.  For a terrible moment I thought that the Naturalist fell, but then I remembered Wraith's smoke bombs were around, so Absolute Zero took heavy damage, but he could take it. We weather through it, and manage to remove all projections and even heal Naturalist thanks to Bestial Shift Shenanigans and sacrificing Natural Born Vigor. 

Start of Dreamer's Turn: 9 cards under her.  Frustrating to say the least, still I know a Toy Master is at the top (infrared eyepiece works on little girl's skulls thankfully,) and I'm not too worried.  Toy Master comes out, another Oni (not good,) an ape (can be dealt with,) and Violent Nightmares. Wraith (2HP) survives thanks to the smoke bombs, but Legacy is not that lucky, he goes down hard.  The team weeps, then takes care of tooth fairy and toy master (why not,) then weeps some more.  Scholar through Zero take their turn just to heal/defend in case Mars has terrible things in plan, it does not, and we win, but at what cost? 

After this game I'm worried. Legacy is what allowed Zero to be such a powerhouse in previous rounds, so my damage output is going down significantly, not to mention my overall team health.  Additionally even though my first team was put together with a lot of thought and attention the backups where chosen with less attention paid to team dynamics, and I think the cracks will begin to show. 

Not to mention the next fight is against the Rat, and an empathic robot is not the tool for that job. 

Well that match goes well enough. Omnitron is still getting his sea legs and wasn't able to keep a component in play, but the others made up for it. Offensive Transmutations and Grappling Hooks are the key to modern medicine, and they kept the team (Sans Zero,) healthy. Much like in the last match against Mr. P. Rat Zero drove himself to the edge making the most he could of the boosts from the infection.  The game ended with tired, but victorious heroes, ready to face down the Chariman again.

posts.name: MigrantP
posts.cooked:
O-M-F-G.

Round Six, Advanced Baron Blade at Rook City.

Things started out well. We smashed the MDP and a Backlash Field right away and were getting Expatriette set up to deal massive damage. The environment wasn't helping but it wasn't hurting too much either, but then the Scum and Villainy started. And Hasten Doom. And Hasten Doom. And Hasten Doom. And Consider the Price of Victory. It made it to a point where we considered whether it would be possible to have BB shuffle his trash into his deck to save the game (he had 5 cards left in his deck). Moon + Earth = lose. We decided to use our mulligan because hey, Baron Blade, we can do this right?

We technically did a little bit better on the second try. But with a Living Force Field and Backlash Field we could not afford to destroy for fear of a Scum and Villainy (which happened, and we would have lost had those been destroyed), by the time we got BB flipped we had 2 incapacitated heroes and the rest at low single digits. All we could do is watch as Scum and Villainy took out all of the rest except Expatriette (via Flak Jacket), then the Ambitious Racketeer finished the job with a sly grin.

B-team, go!

Round Seven, Advanced Citizen Dawn at Ruins of Atlantis.

Stepping up to the plate were Mr. Fixer, The Sentinels, Chrono-Ranger, The Naturalist, and The Wraith. It was a tough draw from the beginning with Citizen Truth, Assault, and Blood+Tears. Autumn came out on the first turn so the Sentinels never got to do much interesting. However, Mr. Fixer kept up steady work, and Chrono-Ranger and The Wraith churned out most of the damage to Dawn thanks to a fortuitous first round Atlantean Font of Power helping us get set up. It came down to the wire with just about every hero target in single digit HP. Three Citizens in the trash and two in play (Autumn and Battery). The Kraken came out and destroyed Battery (who had 2 HP compared to the lowest heroes at 3 HP). On their last legs, the heroes piled on and sent Dawn packing!

Awesome! So I'm about to get my first game going, but I thought I'd review my team and give a little strategy run down before I did so. Here's what I've got.

 

Slot 1: The Controller

Visionry-->Parse-->Tachyon

 

Slot 2: AoE Damage/Utility

Tempest-->Sentinels-->Nightmist

 

Slot 3: The Villain Killer

Ra-->Wraith-->Guise

 

Slot 4: The Tank

Absolute Zero-->Scholar-->Naturalist

 

Slot 5: Team Support

Legacy-->Argent Adept-->Omnitron-X

 

So while I did try to go for a balanced party across the board, I have a plan for the starting roster. The idea here to heavily influence the amount of damage done to my team and the type of damage done accross the field. Between Ra, Visionary, and Legacy, I can change damage to any type I desire and pump my own damage up to crazy amounts. Then I can use that modulated damage to either make Absolute Zero an invincible topped off health tank or a suicide damage murder master. Tempest is there to round off the team with lots of AoE damage and general utility, as I feel Tempest is one of the best heroes in the game and complements any team almost as well as Legacy does. The only thing I'm really worried about with this starting roster is I might not have quite enough ongoing destruction, which I've tried to have the later heroes bring to the table.

The backup heroes are really just some of the best in slot heroes (in my place experience) for each slot. I'm expecting a lot out of each of the 2nd tier heroes if the 1st tier ends up falling. I think the only things I really am sad about in the whole roster is I couldn't find any room for Haka in my game plan and I didn't have enough experience or faith in the WotC heroes to bring them with me.

So time for the first game! Hopefully my fiance and I can take out the Ennead with no casualties. Wish us luck!

posts.name: Wexiomatic
posts.cooked:
Alright, my first two games are in, with surprising results!

Round 1 - vs The Ennead AT Ruins of Atlantis - This was a much harder first match than we were prepared for, as Ra had to face his nemesis. We also got unlucky enough that 4 out of 5 of the Ennead had the green hand symbol, and almost every card the Ennead drew had the green symbol on it. Ra was at half health by the beginning of turn of 2, and it looked grim for him. Legacy's damage boosts slowly wore the Ennead's health down, and Lead from the Front allowed Legacy to soak a lot of the damage meant for Ra. But we didn't pay close enough attention, and Legacy got low enough that one bad turn cost him his life. Still, he managed to play heroic interception before he went down, preventing the death of Ra, and the boost from Galvanize allowed one final turn of increased damage to end the Ennead's reign. Still, loosing Legacy game one was hard on my team, but we honor his sacrifice that kept alive Ra, and move forward with Argent Adept taking his place.

Round 2 - vs Kismet AT Time Cataclysm - A very easy, if high damage, game. I've never thought of Kismet as being very difficult, and this game was no exception. Ann early fueled freeze took out the few ongoing cards Kismet managed to get into play, reducing her threat drastically. Ra also got out Imbued Fire very early in the match and combined with Absolute Zero's Isothermic Transducer, it meant a HUGE amount of fire damage was directed right into Kismet's smug face. I don't even think the game went 5 rounds before it was over and Kismet was defeated. Granted, AZ was at 3 health at the end, but it was still totally worth it. Everyone  pitched in, but in the end it was Ra and Absolute Zero that stole the show this game.

Even with Legacy gone, the team is going strong! Tomorrow we shall tackle the dreamer and see if her hordes of minions overwhelm us (along with her arch enemy), or if we shall stand triumphant!

I don't really have the time to manage all the google docs and stuff, but if anyone wants to set up a VotM Depth Chart event when the time comes, I had started on a semi-random list for the first 15 games if you were to do 3-hero teams. (all expansions/mini-expansions included)  I expanded it to 40 games recently and figured it might help get the ball rolling if anyone wanted to use it. 

 

I did 3 player so you wouldn't have to fiddle with 5 villain turns every round. And so you wouldn't necessarily have to see the same villains back to back.  I think that would more likely happen with 5, since there's only 15 VotM-style villains, including Vengance ones. Another good thing about switching to 3 heroes is that it changes up the strategy a bit from last Depth Chart event.

 

Tried to keep villain teams as unique as possible, with very few instances of the same two villains on the same team (didn't really double check, made this pretty quickly) :

 

1:   Hammer&Anvil -- Fright Train -- La Capitan @ Freedom Tower

2:   Operative -- Baron Blade -- Ambuscade @ Mobile Defense Platform

3:   Bugbear -- Biomancer -- Sgt. Steel @ Rook City

4:   Plague Rat -- Friction -- Greazer @ The Block

5:   Ermine -- Proletariat -- Miss Information @ Temple of Zhu Long

(Every villain has been seen at this point.)

6:   Baron Blade -- Greazer -- Hammer&Anvil @ Tomb of Anubis

7:   Biomancer -- Miss Information -- Operative @ Enclave of the Endlings

8:   Friction -- La Capitan -- Bugbear @ Madame Mittermeier's Fantastical Festival of Conundrums & Curiosities

9:   Proletariat -- Ambuscade -- Plague Rat @ The Celestial Tribunal

10: Fright Train -- Sgt. Steel -- Ermine @ Dok'Thorath

11: Miss Information -- Plague Rat -- Baron Blade @ Realm of Discord

12: La Capitan -- Ermine -- Biomancer @ Insula Primalis

13: Greazer -- Bugbear -- Fright Train @ Ruins of Atlantis

14: Sgt. Steel -- Operative -- Proletariat @ Omnitron IV

15: Ambuscade -- Hammer&Anvil -- Friction @ The Final Wasteland

(The rest, 16-40 are randomized with some slight cherry-picking to prevent too many similar teamups in a row. And I made sure that every villain was on a team with every other villain at least once, and every environment is used at least once.   I'll post the rest later, or PM it to whoever might want to use the rest of the list. Didn't want to make a huge post and break the forums or something. heh)
